    Sampling from a GP posterior¶

    Sampling lets us explore functions compatible with our measurements. We'll start by sampling function values at a fixed set of locations, then draw a function that we can evaluate at new locations and differentiate.

    We use the three observations from First posterior, with measurement-error variance 0.02.

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)

from gpex import (
    FeaturePosteriorPath,
    FunctionalBlock,
    FunctionalDataset,
    FunctionalQuery,
    GaussianProcess,
    ObservationBlock,
    kernels,
    operators,
)

x_observed = jnp.array([[-1.4], [-1.0], [1.2]])
y_observed = jnp.array([-0.8, -0.5, 0.7])

dataset = FunctionalDataset([
    ObservationBlock.from_arrays(
        x_observed, y_observed,
        variance=0.02, name="observed_values", max_size=3,
    )
])
gp = GaussianProcess(
    kernels.RBFKernel(variance=1.0, lengthscale=0.5)
)
posterior = gp.condition(dataset)
    import jax import jax.numpy as jnp jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True) from gpex import ( FeaturePosteriorPath, FunctionalBlock, FunctionalDataset, FunctionalQuery, GaussianProcess, ObservationBlock, kernels, operators, ) x_observed = jnp.array([[-1.4], [-1.0], [1.2]]) y_observed = jnp.array([-0.8, -0.5, 0.7]) dataset = FunctionalDataset([ ObservationBlock.from_arrays( x_observed, y_observed, variance=0.02, name="observed_values", max_size=3, ) ]) gp = GaussianProcess( kernels.RBFKernel(variance=1.0, lengthscale=0.5) ) posterior = gp.condition(dataset)

    Sample values at fixed locations¶

    The posterior function values at any fixed set of locations are jointly Gaussian. We can therefore sample them together from a multivariate Gaussian distribution, preserving their correlations.

    Let's choose nine locations and draw five samples with posterior.sample. The identity operator asks for function values at those locations.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    x_sample = jnp.linspace(-2.0, 2.0, 9)[:, None]
query = FunctionalQuery([
    FunctionalBlock(x_sample, operators.Identity(), name="function")
])
samples = posterior.sample(
    jax.random.key(2), query, sample_count=5
)["function"]
    x_sample = jnp.linspace(-2.0, 2.0, 9)[:, None] query = FunctionalQuery([ FunctionalBlock(x_sample, operators.Identity(), name="function") ]) samples = posterior.sample( jax.random.key(2), query, sample_count=5 )["function"]

    samples has shape (5, 9). Each row is one joint draw, containing a value at each of the nine locations. In the plot, each color shows one row.

    For context, we'll show the posterior mean and pointwise 95% intervals in the background. predict_marginals computes the means and variances needed for this band.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    x_plot = jnp.linspace(-2.0, 2.0, 101)[:, None]
function_query = FunctionalQuery([
    FunctionalBlock(x_plot, operators.Identity(), name="function")
])
function_posterior = posterior.predict_marginals(function_query)
    x_plot = jnp.linspace(-2.0, 2.0, 101)[:, None] function_query = FunctionalQuery([ FunctionalBlock(x_plot, operators.Identity(), name="function") ]) function_posterior = posterior.predict_marginals(function_query)
    In [4]:
    plotting-setup
    Copied! 
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.rcParams.update({
    "figure.figsize": (8, 3.8),
    "figure.dpi": 120,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.18,
    "font.size": 10,
})


def plot_posterior(ax, x, prediction, name):
    mean = prediction.mean[name]
    sd = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(prediction.variance[name], 0.0))
    ax.fill_between(
        x, mean - 1.96 * sd, mean + 1.96 * sd,
        color="#1F4E79", alpha=0.12, linewidth=0,
        label="95% posterior interval", zorder=0,
    )
    ax.plot(
        x, mean, color="#1F4E79", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2,
        alpha=0.7, label="Posterior mean", zorder=1,
    )


def plot_draws(ax, x, other_draws, highlighted):
    for i, values in enumerate(other_draws):
        ax.plot(
            x, values, color="#6D597A", linewidth=0.9, alpha=0.3,
            label="Other draws" if i == 0 else None,
        )
    ax.plot(
        x, highlighted, color="#6D597A", linewidth=1.8,
        label="Highlighted draw", zorder=3,
    )
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt plt.rcParams.update({ "figure.figsize": (8, 3.8), "figure.dpi": 120, "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": 0.18, "font.size": 10, }) def plot_posterior(ax, x, prediction, name): mean = prediction.mean[name] sd = jnp.sqrt(jnp.maximum(prediction.variance[name], 0.0)) ax.fill_between( x, mean - 1.96 * sd, mean + 1.96 * sd, color="#1F4E79", alpha=0.12, linewidth=0, label="95% posterior interval", zorder=0, ) ax.plot( x, mean, color="#1F4E79", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.2, alpha=0.7, label="Posterior mean", zorder=1, ) def plot_draws(ax, x, other_draws, highlighted): for i, values in enumerate(other_draws): ax.plot( x, values, color="#6D597A", linewidth=0.9, alpha=0.3, label="Other draws" if i == 0 else None, ) ax.plot( x, highlighted, color="#6D597A", linewidth=1.8, label="Highlighted draw", zorder=3, )
    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(layout="constrained")
plot_posterior(ax, x_plot[:, 0], function_posterior, "function")
colors = ["#1F4E79", "#6D597A", "#2A7F7F", "#A23B4A", "#7B6B2D"]
for i, values in enumerate(samples):
    ax.scatter(
        x_sample[:, 0], values,
        color=colors[i], s=25, label=f"Draw {i + 1}", zorder=3,
    )
ax.scatter(
    x_observed[:, 0], y_observed,
    color="#D97706", marker="x", s=55, label="Measurements", zorder=4,
)
ax.set(xlabel="Location", ylabel="Sampled function value")
fig.legend(loc="outside lower center", ncol=4, frameon=False, fontsize=9)
plt.show()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(layout="constrained") plot_posterior(ax, x_plot[:, 0], function_posterior, "function") colors = ["#1F4E79", "#6D597A", "#2A7F7F", "#A23B4A", "#7B6B2D"] for i, values in enumerate(samples): ax.scatter( x_sample[:, 0], values, color=colors[i], s=25, label=f"Draw {i + 1}", zorder=3, ) ax.scatter( x_observed[:, 0], y_observed, color="#D97706", marker="x", s=55, label="Measurements", zorder=4, ) ax.set(xlabel="Location", ylabel="Sampled function value") fig.legend(loc="outside lower center", ncol=4, frameon=False, fontsize=9) plt.show()

    The uncertainty grows in the large gap between the observations. The samples reflect this by spreading out more there.

    This gives us values at the chosen locations. If we want a sample on a finer fixed grid, we can include that whole grid in the query and sample its values jointly.

    Sample a function¶

    A GP is also a distribution over functions. We can draw a function and then evaluate it wherever we need, including locations chosen after the draw.

    FeaturePosteriorPath gives us an approximate function draw. Larger feature_count values improve the approximation on average, but make the function slower to evaluate.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    f_sample = FeaturePosteriorPath(
    posterior, jax.random.key(7), feature_count=1024
)
    f_sample = FeaturePosteriorPath( posterior, jax.random.key(7), feature_count=1024 )

    f_sample takes one location and returns one value. For example, in this one-dimensional problem we can evaluate it at 0.25 by passing an array with one entry.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    print(f"f(0.25) = {f_sample(jnp.array([0.25])):.3f}")
    print(f"f(0.25) = {f_sample(jnp.array([0.25])):.3f}")
    f(0.25) = 0.467

    To plot this function, use jax.vmap to evaluate it across the plotting grid. We can also evaluate the same draw at new locations between the grid points.

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    function_values = jax.vmap(f_sample)(x_plot)

new_locations = jnp.array([[-0.75], [0.25], [1.75]])
new_values = jax.vmap(f_sample)(new_locations)
    function_values = jax.vmap(f_sample)(x_plot) new_locations = jnp.array([[-0.75], [0.25], [1.75]]) new_values = jax.vmap(f_sample)(new_locations)

    Differentiate the sampled function¶

    We can apply operators to the sampled function. Here the RBF kernel gives smooth functions, so we can use jax.grad to differentiate it. Our input has one coordinate, so each gradient has one component: the derivative with respect to location.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    df_sample = jax.grad(f_sample)
derivative_values = jax.vmap(df_sample)(x_plot)[:, 0]
    df_sample = jax.grad(f_sample) derivative_values = jax.vmap(df_sample)(x_plot)[:, 0]

    Let's add eleven more function draws to see how their values and derivatives vary. For the derivative plot's background, PartialDerivative asks the GP for the derivative mean and variance directly.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    derivative_query = FunctionalQuery([
    FunctionalBlock(
        x_plot, operators.PartialDerivative(axis=0), name="derivative"
    )
])
derivative_posterior = posterior.predict_marginals(derivative_query)
    derivative_query = FunctionalQuery([ FunctionalBlock( x_plot, operators.PartialDerivative(axis=0), name="derivative" ) ]) derivative_posterior = posterior.predict_marginals(derivative_query)
    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    other_values = []
other_derivatives = []
for key in jax.random.split(jax.random.key(8), 11):
    draw = FeaturePosteriorPath(posterior, key, feature_count=1024)
    other_values.append(jax.vmap(draw)(x_plot))
    other_derivatives.append(jax.vmap(jax.grad(draw))(x_plot)[:, 0])
    other_values = [] other_derivatives = [] for key in jax.random.split(jax.random.key(8), 11): draw = FeaturePosteriorPath(posterior, key, feature_count=1024) other_values.append(jax.vmap(draw)(x_plot)) other_derivatives.append(jax.vmap(jax.grad(draw))(x_plot)[:, 0])
    In [12]:
    Copied! 
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.5, 4.2), layout="constrained")
plot_posterior(axes[0], x_plot[:, 0], function_posterior, "function")
plot_draws(axes[0], x_plot[:, 0], other_values, function_values)
axes[0].scatter(
    new_locations[:, 0], new_values, color="#6D597A", edgecolors="white",
    s=35, zorder=4, label="New evaluations",
)
axes[0].scatter(
    x_observed[:, 0], y_observed,
    color="#D97706", marker="x", s=55, zorder=4, label="Measurements",
)
axes[0].set(title="Sampled functions", xlabel="Location", ylabel="Function value")

plot_posterior(axes[1], x_plot[:, 0], derivative_posterior, "derivative")
plot_draws(axes[1], x_plot[:, 0], other_derivatives, derivative_values)
axes[1].axhline(0.0, color="0.5", linewidth=0.6, alpha=0.5)
axes[1].set(title="Their derivatives", xlabel="Location", ylabel="Derivative")

handles, labels = axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
fig.legend(
    handles, labels, loc="outside lower center",
    ncol=3, frameon=False, fontsize=9,
)
plt.show()
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.5, 4.2), layout="constrained") plot_posterior(axes[0], x_plot[:, 0], function_posterior, "function") plot_draws(axes[0], x_plot[:, 0], other_values, function_values) axes[0].scatter( new_locations[:, 0], new_values, color="#6D597A", edgecolors="white", s=35, zorder=4, label="New evaluations", ) axes[0].scatter( x_observed[:, 0], y_observed, color="#D97706", marker="x", s=55, zorder=4, label="Measurements", ) axes[0].set(title="Sampled functions", xlabel="Location", ylabel="Function value") plot_posterior(axes[1], x_plot[:, 0], derivative_posterior, "derivative") plot_draws(axes[1], x_plot[:, 0], other_derivatives, derivative_values) axes[1].axhline(0.0, color="0.5", linewidth=0.6, alpha=0.5) axes[1].set(title="Their derivatives", xlabel="Location", ylabel="Derivative") handles, labels = axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels() fig.legend( handles, labels, loc="outside lower center", ncol=3, frameon=False, fontsize=9, ) plt.show()

    The functions agree more closely near the measurements and vary more widely in the large gap. The darker function and derivative belong to the same draw: the derivative is positive where that function increases and negative where it decreases.

    Reuse f_sample when you need more evaluations or derivatives of this draw. Construct it with a new random key when you want to sample another function.
